doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: Meeting his wife Jill
summary: He first saw Jill at 15 at a Montgomery Wards radio broadcast, then met her again through Tony Madonia, her brother-in-law, and recalls a Birdland incident.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Wow. Did you meet Jill [his wife] in high school?

I saw Jill when I was 15 years old. I was on a gig at Montgomery Wards in Rome, a live radio broadcast with Al Serway and Joe Abbis and Anthony Elliot, the great cellist, who was playing bass in those days, and Dave Derby was the announcer. How’s that for remembering something.
Where are you going this afternoon? Do you remember that? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-

No I don’t even know where I am right now. But yeah, so I saw Jill. She was with her then-boyfriend and I knew him. We were playing in this tent at Montgomery Wards in Rome in the parking lot at some kind of grand opening or something. And she came in with him and immediately it was like oh my Lord, you know, who is that? How can I get next to her? You know. And then I didn’t see her for another three years. But I thought about her for three years. And then I started playing with a saxophone player by the name of Tony Madonia. I don’t know if you remember him, Monk.

You might have. He died very early, and he might have been around when you first came into Rome, right around that time maybe he passed away. But I started playing in his band and as it turned out Tony was married to Jill’s sister and they lived in a duplex house and Jill lived on the other side. And when I was pulling into his house she came out on the porch and my world changed.
I remember some anecdote about you jumping over the organ or something at Birdland to defend her honor or something like that.
I’m not going to go into the details. I was a little tougher in those days and a little stupider. Stupider?
